subject: Deployment mode and pricing follow-up — Acme AI
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Martinez <sofia@acme.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-28T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: Deployment mode follow-up and next steps — Acme AI

Hi Sofia,

Thanks again for the time today — great conversation. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our discovery:

- Primary goal: low-latency customer-facing chat for Acme's support product (multi-tenant SaaS).
- Estimated steady-state traffic: ~500 RPS at peak, ~200 RPS average.
- Latency SLO: 150-200ms p95 for short chats (<=512 tokens).
- Data requirements: PII redaction and SOC 2 controls; some logs must stay within your VPC (HIPAA not required today).

You mentioned three deployment modes are of interest: Hosted API (fastest to ship), Dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pools for predictable throughput), and Private (VPC/on-prem) for stricter network controls. You asked for a cost comparison and a simple break-even analysis between per-token hosted pricing and reserved-capacity economics.

I've attached a short pricing spreadsheet that walks through three scenarios and a couple of example usage profiles. High-level guidance below; we can run this against your actual usage data if you share a sample-week token histogram.

Hosted API (per-token):
- Pros: no infra commitments, immediate onboarding, built-in autoscaling and fallbacks.
- Cons: higher marginal cost at scale; less control over custom SKUs/quantization.
- Example price assumptions in sheet: $0.00035 / gen-token; embeddings $0.00012 / embedding.
- Economics: good for proof-of-concept and low-to-medium volume. Break-even typically at ~2–4M tokens/month depending on SLA/throughput needs.

Dedicated capacity (reserved):
- Pros: predictable throughput, lower per-token equivalent cost when heavily utilized, stronger isolation.
- Cons: commit required (monthly/annual), warm-up time for large caches.
- Typical committed model: reserved capacity price + usage at a much lower per-token compute rate. Example: $12k/month reserved pool for a baseline capacity of X throughput (see sheet) + included token allowance; incremental tokens billed at a discounted rate.

Private (VPC / on-prem):
- Pros: full network control, customer-managed egress, integration with KMS/HSM, suitable for regulated workloads.
- Cons: one-time setup, higher baseline ops/maintenance, longer lead time.

Next steps I propose:
1) I’ll tailor the attached spreadsheet to your expected token distribution if you can share a 7-day sample (anonymized).
2) Marissa (cc'd) can run a quick capacity estimate for Dedicated based on your 500 RPS peak and token sizes.
3) If you want pricing for Private VPC/on-prem, Neha (cc'd) can outline setup fees and typical timelines.

Attachments: Redwood-pricing-commit-options.xlsx (spreadsheet)

Would you be able to share a week of anonymized request logs (token counts per request) or approve us using the example profile in the sheet?

Thanks,

Aditya Rao
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Thanks Aditya — appreciate the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side:

- We are leaning toward Dedicated capacity because of predictable latency and isolation requirements.
- Peak estimate: 500 RPS is correct for product peak (concurrent active users ~ 25k). Average payloads are ~150 tokens/request gen + 40 tokens/context; embeddings are occasional for search tuning (~50k/month).
- Procurement questions: what committed term lengths do you offer (monthly vs annual)? Are there volume discounts for multi-quarter commits? Also need an estimate of the minimum committed spend so our finance team can prepare a PO.

I can share a 7-day anonymized token histogram today if that helps — attaching to a reply now. For now please assume monthly commits preferred; we’ll consider annual if the delta is compelling.

Sofia Martinez

sofia@acme.ai

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Martinez <sofia@acme.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-30T11:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Deployment mode follow-up and next steps — Acme AI

Great — thanks for the histogram, Sofia. I ran the spreadsheet against the profile you shared and summarized the outcomes below (high-level):

Scenario A — Hosted API (per-token):
- Assumptions: 10M gen tokens/month, embeddings 50k/month.
- Estimated monthly cost: ~$3,500 (generation) + ~$6 (embeddings) = ~$3,506.
- Pros: no commit; simple line item.

Scenario B — Dedicated (monthly reserved):
- Assumptions: commit equivalent to a small dedicated pool sized for your 500 RPS peak. Example reserved pool price in sheet: $12,000/month includes baseline throughput and 20M tokens/month included. Incremental tokens after allowance billed at $0.00012 per token.
- If you average 10–15M tokens/month, effective cost after commit can be lower or similar to hosted, but you gain throughput guarantees and isolation.
- Break-even: for your profile, Dedicated becomes attractive at sustained usage > ~8M gen tokens/month with the given pricing assumptions.

Scenario C — Private (VPC/on-prem):
- One-time setup: $40k (integration & security carve-outs) + annual platform license (example $60k/year) + infra (customer-managed or via runbook).
- Good fit if you require VPC-isolated logs and on-prem constraints; not recommended for initial pilot due to lead time.

Other notes:
- We can do monthly reserved commits or annual prepay with meaningful discounts (typical annual uplift 10–25% savings over monthly billing).
- We can include an autoscaling burst allowance for traffic spikes; details in the spreadsheet.
- For procurement, Neha can provide a minimum committed spend figure and standard contract templates.

I also attached a quick model of sensitivity: if your tokens/month go up to 20M, Dedicated yields ~35–45% savings vs hosted under these assumptions. If you stay under 5M tokens/month, hosted is cheaper and lower friction.

Attachments: Redwood-pricing-commit-options.xlsx

Would you like us to produce a short one-page term sheet for a monthly committed Dedicated option so procurement can review? If so, I’ll loop in legal and Neha to prepare an indicative term sheet and PO-ready numbers.

Best,

Aditya Rao
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-03-31T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Deployment mode follow-up and next steps — Acme AI

Hi Sofia — quick tech note from the engineering side to help with sizing and costs:

- For 500 RPS peak with ~190 tokens/request average, we recommend a 2-node dedicated pool (NVIDIA A100 equivalent or similar) configured with our continuous batching and KV cache enabled. That configuration handles the 150–200ms p95 target for short chats.
- Cache warm-up: with chat workloads you’ll see improved per-token cost after the KV cache matures; I included a warm-up curve in the spreadsheet (weeks 0–4).
- Quantization: if you can accept int8 for some model variants we can reduce GPU memory and increase packing density; this impacts licensing and sometimes a small quality delta — happy to run evals.
- For Private VPC, network egress and dedicated KMS integration adds ~2–3 weeks to delivery and the one-time setup fee noted by Aditya.

If you’re happy with the Dedicated direction, we can produce an SRE-ready runbook and SLA appendix to include in the term sheet.

-Marissa
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
